solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soup recipe ingested by artist

indicators.note: something ingested is swallowed, so it ends up inside the word that follows

parts.note: Hieronymus Bosch, the Dutch painter
R is the standard abbreviation for recipe (Latin 'take') on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A painter swallowing the instructions for making soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recipe' looks like it belongs with the soup, but it is the prescription abbreviation from Latin 'take'.
explanation.definitionFit: Borsch (borscht) is the beetroot soup of Russia and Ukraine.

clue.text: Chancy investment wild eclat tucked up — owlish maybe?

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order
tucked up means snug in a bed, so the other pieces lie inside

parts.note: someone tucked up is in bed
spec is short for speculation, a risky venture
the letters of the word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild speculative bet tucked away by someone who looks wise as an owl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked up' does double duty: it gives the bed and says the rest goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are pictured with round eyes like spectacles, so an owlish look is one example of being bespectacled.

clue.text: A pistol cocked? Rule of order

indicators.note: cocked means tilted upwards, and in a down clue that flips the letters to read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
the Luger is a German automatic pistol

explanation.surface: A gun is cocked, and someone calls a point of order.
explanation.definitionFit: A regula is the written rule of a religious order, such as the Rule of St Benedict.

clue.text: Runner? Plenty turned up in advance

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means flipped to read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: lots means plenty
on means ahead or forward

explanation.surface: An athlete arriving in large numbers ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete; it is the botanical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolon is a runner in botany: a creeping stem that roots to form a new plant, as in strawberries.

clue.text: Cheesy stuff given a whirl within? It's revolting

indicators.note: a whirl turns things round, and 'within' limits it to the middle of the word

parts.note: curd is the solid part of soured milk, used for cheese

explanation.surface: A cheese someone tried turned out disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the two middle letters swap round; the outer C and D stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: Crud is slang for anything filthy or disgusting, so it is something revolting.

clue.text: Old time tart, head dropping somewhat

indicators.note: the leading letter slips down a little way, moving the start of the word round

parts.note: tart is slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: An old-time tart, her head drooping a little.
explanation.walkthrough: The W at the head moves down two places, behind H and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Howre is an old spelling of hour, used by Spenser; 'Old' flags the archaic form of a unit of time.

clue.text: Everything within that kiss stirred divine femininity

indicators.note: something stirred is mixed about, so the kept letters are rearranged
all the letters lying inside, so every letter except the two ends is kept

parts.note: the phrase without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A passionate kiss that awakened a goddess-like feminine spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everything within' means the whole of the phrase bar its outer letters, here T and S.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism Shakti is the female creative energy of the cosmos, personified as the consort of a god.

clue.text: My husband coos when dancing cheek to cheek?

indicators.note: dancing moves the letters around the floor into new positions

parts.note: taken as written
h is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman's husband murmurs sweet nothings while they dance close.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoochy describes romantic slow music or dancing done in a close embrace, faces touching.

clue.text: Toxic latex, not for a tip of rubber

parts.note: anti means against, not in favour of
taken as written

indicators.note: the tip is the very first point, so just the opening letter is used

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A poisonous latex is no use for the end of a rubber.
explanation.definitionFit: The antiar is the upas tree of Java, and its poisonous latex was used on arrow tips.

clue.text: Arak drunk with 'io', a foreign toast

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters lurch out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Arak is drunk to a cry of 'io' as someone abroad raises a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: Arak is a spirit, and io a classical shout of triumph, which fits the drinking scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Kia ora is a Maori greeting wishing good health, used as a toast in New Zealand.

clue.text: Shipworm mostly found under matting in shreds

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
in a down clue being under means coming after in the answer

parts.note: tat is a coarse Indian matting or canvas
the teredo is a boring mollusc that eats ship timbers

explanation.surface: A shipworm has chewed some matting to ribbons.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattered means torn into rags and shreds.

clue.text: Members of front line showing hunches about dire suffering (12, two words)

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: an insight is an intuitive hunch

indicators.note: suffering things are in a bad way, so these letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: the letters of the word, rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers in the front line have dark feelings about terrible hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front line' suggests war, but it is the forward line of a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: In old football formations the inside rights were forwards, playing between centre forward and right wing.

clue.text: Was introduced to gypsy, one showing passion for versifying

parts.note: to have met someone is to have been introduced
the Romani people, once commonly called gypsies
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone meets a Romani poet who displays a passion for writing verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Metromania is a mania for writing poetry, from metre plus mania.

clue.text: Bright Californian plant I placed alongside square

indicators.note: set next to means the two parts simply sit side by side

parts.note: S is short for square, as in measurements
the ego is the self, the 'I'

explanation.surface: A gardener describes setting a vivid Californian plant beside a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: The sego lily is a brightly flowered bulb of the western United States, the state flower of Utah.

clue.text: Society puts finger on key figures

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society
Chambers gives tat as a verb meaning to touch or tap lightly

explanation.surface: A society identifying the important numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: TAT here is a rare verb found in Chambers, the Azed dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Stats is the informal clipping of statistics, the important numbers in a report.

clue.text: Spread lard upon detachable plate

indicators.note: spreading something moves its parts about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to smear fat on a removable dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plate' suggests crockery, which suits the lard, but it is a piece of armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pauldron is the separate piece of plate armour covering a knight's shoulder.

clue.text: Coach circumventing what may be Indian gazelle

indicators.note: to circumvent is literally to go round, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: chara is short for charabanc, an old motor coach
Indian ink is a dense black ink

explanation.surface: A coach takes the long way round what might be an Indian antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' seems to go with gazelle, but belongs to the ink.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinkara is a small gazelle of India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Announced month left once given judgement

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
L is the abbreviation for left
ared is an obsolete past form of aread, to judge or interpret; 'once' marks it archaic

explanation.surface: A verdict was announced a month after someone left.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something is to announce it formally.

clue.text: Shell in pieces for bangles, 100 on loop

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
a hank is a coil or loop of yarn or rope

explanation.surface: A jeweller cuts a shell into pieces and strings a hundred bangles on a loop.
explanation.definitionFit: The chank is a large Indian sea shell cut into rings to make bangles.

clue.text: Figure congaed unrestrainedly

indicators.note: without restraint the letters move freely and land in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A figure danced the conga wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' reads as a person or a dance move; it is a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a plane shape with ten sides, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Ambassador maybe providing enclosure for sandarach in African capital

indicators.note: to enclose something is to surround it, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is how an ambassador is styled
the arar is the sandarach tree of north Africa

explanation.surface: An envoy keeps a stock of resin in an African capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Harare is the capital city of Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Cocktail of Pepsi and Lilt? This is primarily 'lite' possibly

indicators.note: possibly marks one possible arrangement: the letters of the drinks could be reordered as this plus the others

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; Lilt is a British fruit soft drink
taken as written, to be taken away

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

parts.note: the first letter, also to be taken away

explanation.surface: Mixing Pepsi with Lilt, a fruit soda, would hardly make a strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: 'This' stands for the answer, and THIS + IS + L is an anagram of PEPSI LILT, so take IS and L out of those letters to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipple is an alcoholic drink, so a cocktail is one example.

clue.text: Haggle, requiring penny change

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for penny
to alter is to change

explanation.surface: Bargaining down to the last penny of change.
explanation.definitionFit: Palter, in an older sense, means to haggle or bargain over terms.

clue.text: Wearing armour, ready to serve?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: covered in metal plates
second meaning: food put on the plate

explanation.walkthrough: Serving suggests a knight in armour serving a king; the second sense is a meal ready to go out.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight in plate armour is plated, and food set out on plates in a kitchen is plated.

clue.text: Child dropped subject more ready to learn

indicators.note: something dropped is let go, so those letters fall out of the word

parts.note: a chapter is a division of a book dealing with one subject
ch is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A child gave up a school subject, being quicker to pick things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt can mean quick to learn, so apter is the comparative: readier to grasp things.

clue.text: Pair of friends showing what's need to deal with sensation?

definitions.text: what's need to deal with sensation

wordplay.note: pal means friend, so two of them

explanation.surface: Two friends who have what it takes to handle a sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'need' stands for 'needed'. A palp is the feeler an insect uses to sense things.
explanation.definitionFit: Palpal means relating to palps, the sense organs an insect uses for touch and taste.

clue.text: University shows this ivy's disfigured … Trinity?

indicators.note: something disfigured has its shape spoilt, so the letters are mixed into another shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be taken away

explanation.surface: A university, its ivy defaced, is Trinity College perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: 'this' stands for the answer, and THIS + IVYS jumbled makes UNIVERSITY, so take IVYS out of those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Triune means three in one, the defining nature of the Holy Trinity.

clue.text: Literary bits and pieces smart chap penned in column?

indicators.note: penned in means shut inside an enclosure, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: an anta is a pilaster or square column at the end of a wall
a smart alec is a know-all

explanation.surface: A newspaper column containing snippets of writing by a clever fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' looks like a newspaper column; it is an architectural one.
explanation.definitionFit: Analecta are collected literary extracts or gleanings, a set of fragments.

clue.text: Silly, appearing regularly in tow, de trop

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: every second letter, starting from the third

explanation.surface: A foolish hanger-on who is unwanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' is a noun here, as in 'you silly'. De trop is French for unwelcome or in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or contemptible person, so the noun silly is a synonym.

clue.text: Corvid with dead fish, in no hurry?

parts.note: the daw or jackdaw is a member of the crow family
d is the abbreviation for dead
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A jackdaw lingers over a dead fish, unhurried.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawdling means moving slowly and idly, taking your time.

clue.text: Work at good English for magistrate

parts.note: to do something is to work at it
g is the abbreviation for good
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Working at good English to become a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: The doge was the chief magistrate of the old republics of Venice and Genoa.

clue.text: Coffee dish, edges spilt

indicators.note: with the edges spilt, the outer letters are lost and only the inside stays

parts.note: a platter is a large serving dish

explanation.surface: Coffee slops over the rim of a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is espresso coffee made with plenty of steamed milk.

clue.text: Advance turned up — not a word

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the word that follows reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written
sh is a call for silence, not another word

explanation.surface: Someone moved forward, silently.
explanation.definitionFit: To push is to press forward or advance, as an army does.

clue.text: Take one's grade playing keyboard instruments (10, two words)

parts.note: R, from Latin recipe, means take, as on prescriptions

indicators.note: the letters are played around with and so come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A music student sits an exam on the keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take one's grade' reads like sitting a music exam, but 'Take' is the prescription abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Reed organs, such as the harmonium, are keyboard instruments sounded by vibrating reeds.

clue.text: Leaders of stricken town abandoned tattered standard, Trojan

indicators.note: something tattered is torn to pieces, so the remaining letters are jumbled
abandoned means left behind, so those letters are taken away
leaders go in front, so only the opening letters of the next words count

parts.note: first letters of the two words
taken as written

explanation.surface: In a ravaged city a Trojan leaves behind a torn flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Dardan, after Dardanus, founder of Troy, is a poetic word for Trojan.

clue.text: Hero's father — matter involves dodgy 'eel'!

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or out of order, so these letters get rearranged
to involve is to wrap up inside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: pus is the matter that oozes from an infection
the letters of the word, jumbled

explanation.surface: A dubious eel turns up in a story about a hero's dad.
explanation.walkthrough: The hero is Achilles, son of Peleus and the sea nymph Thetis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Peleus was king of the Myrmidons and father of Achilles.
